title: fix(scripts): tenant-audit census stores declared type text as written, and resolves names by scope
body:
Fixes #19300

Two defects in one file's TypeScript reading, with two independent fixes. Route ① for
the first, as triage on the predecessor card named it; scope-keyed name resolution for
the second.

## Defect 1 — the census collapsed declared type text before re-parsing it

`declaredTypesIn` stored a declared type through `getText(sf).replace(/\s+/g, ' ')`. The
door rule is later read off that text by re-parsing it as a synthetic alias
(`type CensusReceiver = THE_STORED_TEXT;`). A type literal may separate its members by
a NEWLINE alone — legal TypeScript — and the collapse turns that separator into nothing,
so the synthesis does not parse and the site is refused as
`type-text-not-round-trippable`. The author was told to restyle legal TypeScript to work
around the tool's own re-serialisation.

The text is now stored exactly as the source spells it. The collapse was never needed at
the storage boundary: every reader of that text either scans it for identifiers or
re-parses it, and the one place a single line is genuinely required — the artefacts —
already collapses at the point of render (`runCensus`, `cell()`).

**The real site set is TWO, not the three the card names.** Measured on this branch:

| site | in the set? | why |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `note()`'s `type` field | **yes** | feeds `readTypeTextDoor` through `fromEntry` |
| the `shapes` member type | **yes** | feeds it through `memberTypeOfShapes` |
| `receiverKey` | no | a receiver's own spelling, for ledger keys and diagnostics; never re-parsed |
| `note()`'s `init` field | no | a diagnostic, truncated to 120 chars; scanned by regex, never re-parsed |
| the `as` path's `r.type.getText(sf)` | no | never collapsed in the first place — it is the lit control that already proved raw text round-trips |
| the spread / opaque / runtime-name sites | no | diagnostics and object names, never type texts |
| `:355` in `memberIsEngineDoor` | no | `replace(/\s+/g, '')` — an **empty** replacement, and its only consumer is `t !== 'string'`. It normalises for an equality test and is never handed to a parser. |

## Defect 2 — `locals` was keyed by bare identifier, with no scope

A file may contain several `engine`s. Keyed on the identifier alone they were one entry,
and the first TYPED one decided for all of them. That is **three** failures, not one, and
which one you get depends on declaration order:

| shape | before | after |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| engine-typed `engine` declared first, `Map` second | `Map.delete` scored an **engine write** and admitted to the certified population | the Map is subtracted |
| `Map` first, engine-typed second | the **real engine write** subtracted as `platform-type` — a DEFENDED arm, so it prints nothing and is counted nowhere | the engine write is placed |
| both engine-typed, one unreadable | both refused (the card's measured instance) | both placed |

The middle row is the expensive one and the card does not name it: the census's own header
calls a silent subtraction the direction it cannot survive being wrong in, and the
bare-name map was producing them.

The conflation also decided two other verdicts the artefacts carry — **which object** a
site writes (`resolveObjectNameArg`) and **whether it is elevated** (`elevationOf`). Both
are pinned now.

`declaredTypesIn` resolves a name through its innermost enclosing scope, with the old
file-wide map kept as an explicit floor tier: consulted only when no enclosing scope
declares the name, so **no receiver that resolved before stops resolving**.

## What this moves on the real corpus

The population is unchanged — **227 sites before, 227 after, none added, none removed**.
Fourteen sites change attribution, and one receiver becomes honestly unreadable:

- 6 sites stop needing an `UNTYPED_RECEIVERS` row (the census can now read their declared
  type), so three ledger rows are deleted as stale.
- 2 sites in `bootstrap-declared-webhooks.ts` resolve their object name to `sys_webhook`
  for the first time — `undecidable` becomes `enabled`.
- 6 sites in `metadata-store.ts` move from `declared-type` to the object-name rescue.
  Their receiver is a **contextually typed** arrow parameter (`(engine) => engine.insert(…)`
  against a declared `run: (engine: IDataEngine) => …`), which needs a type checker this
  module does not have. The bare-name map had been answering it from an unrelated
  declaration and happened to be right; the verdict is unchanged either way.
- 1 receiver — `const db = context.database` in `auth-manager.ts` — was being answered by a
  a `Record` keyed by string declared 2000 lines away and silently subtracted as
  `platform-type`. It is the better-auth adapter bound to the SCIM transaction, and it
  arrives in `UNTYPED_RECEIVERS` saying so.

## ✅ Closed: the artefacts are regenerated in this PR

This PR's originally declared file surface was `scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs` plus its
self-test and fixtures, and the defect-2 repair moves the census totals, which stales the
committed artefacts. The dev **stopped at that fence and declared the red** rather than
widening silently. The seat then **widened the fence** — the artefacts ride the source PR
rather than a follow-up card, per the lane rule 「其重生成的 references 产物归源 PR」.

Both steps are done:

1. `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write` regenerated
   `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx` and
   `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md`.
2. The hand-written prose numbers `--write` does not touch were taken **from the gate's own
   output**, not retyped from any summary: `const` 41→43, unreadable-and-tenancy-enabled
   32→34 (twice), statically decidable 151→153, undecidable 76→74.

`check-tenant-audit-census.mjs` and its `--self-test` are now **green (27/27, up from 6
failing)**, which also confirms the diagnosis: all six failures were the drift.

**Defect 1 is artefact-neutral and was measured as such**: with only the two storage-site
lines changed, the census `--json` is byte-identical to the base tree (`diff` exit 0 over
the full document). Every count that moves comes from defect 2.

## Verification

All **66** gates `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands`
derives for the widened diff were run and reconciled with `--ran` on the final head:
**66 derived / 66 run / 0 NOT MEASURED / 0 UNRUN, every family carrying a recorded exit
code, all zero.** The set grew from 29 because the diff now reaches `content/docs/**`,
`docs/audits/**` and `ts-parse.mjs`.

⚠️ Five families first returned PREREQUISITE NOT MET (three needing `@objectstack/lint`
built, one `packages/spec/json-schema`, one `@objectstack/client-react` declarations).
They were recorded as **NOT MEASURED, never as clean**, and re-measured to exit 0 after
two builds through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`.

Reverse verification — three ablations through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, each run
from the committed state with the on-disk mutation proven and the restore verified
`blob == HEAD` with `git diff HEAD` empty:

| ablation | red |
| :--- | :--- |
| re-collapse `note()`'s `type` | 3 of 67 — the inline, parameter-annotation and non-door newline cases |
| re-collapse the `shapes` member type | 1 of 67 — the interface-member case only, proving the two storage sites are independently reached |
| drop the lexical tier, leave only the floor | 4 of 67 — both declaration orders, the object name and the elevation |

The self-test grows 57 to 67 cases. The `type-text-not-round-trippable` arm is **kept and
still exercised**: a genuinely unparseable text is still refused and still places nothing.
What changed is what it means — it is now the alarm for a defect in this module's own
re-serialisation, never an instruction to restyle the corpus, and the refusal text says so.

## Acceptance notes

- ✅ **`scripts/check-tenant-audit-census.mjs`'s refusal prescription** ("spell the
  literal's members with `;` separators so the stored text round-trips") was made false by
  this change and is the copy CI prints. **Fixed in this PR** — text only. It no longer
  asks the author to restyle anything; it says the fault is the census's own and to file it
  there.
- ✅ **`scripts/ts-parse.mjs`'s header** documented the collapse as a live defect. **Fixed
  in this PR** — text only, now historical. ⛔ It deliberately does NOT retire the door it
  documents: the measurement is a fact about the PARSER, which has not changed, and any
  caller re-parsing text it synthesised itself can fail the same way.
- **The same conflation survives one map over**, and it is reproducible today. Two classes
  in one file sharing a property name: `class B`'s `this.engine.delete('k')` on a
  a `Map` of string to number scores `engine/IProbeEngine` — a `Map` admitted to the certified
  tenancy population. `fnReturns` behaves the same way for two same-named local functions.
  `thisProps` needs CLASS scope rather than lexical scope, which is a different notion from
  the one this PR adds, so it is reported rather than folded in. **Filed by the seat as
  #19652.**
- **Contextually typed parameters are unreadable to this census**, before and after — see
  the `metadata-store.ts` note above. A capability gap, not a regression; recorded so the
  6 sites' move to the object-name rescue is not read as one.
- **This change makes #19299 acutely live.** That card is the census self-test's
  clean-census control being coupled to the live tree through `refuse`. The coupling was
  latent while the tree was clean; with the artefacts drifted, **6 of the gate's 27
  self-test cases now fail, and 5 of them are controls** asserting that a stale number is
  NOT a finding. They fail for the reason they exist to deny. ⛔ Not folded in — it is a
  different defect and deliberately serialised behind this card.
